displayedInputs.question: In quadrilateral \(ABCD\), \(AB=CD\), \(AD=CB\), and \(\angle B=70^\circ\). Find the measure of \(\angle D\) in degrees.
If two triangles have two pairs of equal sides and one pair of equal angles, are they necessarily congruent?

choices.B: Not necessarily; the angle must be the included angle between the two sides
choices.D: They are necessarily congruent by SSA

displayedInputs.question: In \(\triangle ABC\) and \(\triangle DEF\), \(AB=DE\), \(\angle B=\angle E\), and \(BC=EF\). Which criterion establishes that they are congruent?
In \(\triangle ABC\) and \(\triangle DEF\), \(AB=DE\) and \(AC=DF\). Which additional condition allows the two triangles to be proved congruent by SAS?
Segments \(AC\) and \(BD\) intersect at point \(O\), with \(OA=OC\), \(OB=OD\), and \(AB=7\). Find the length of \(CD\).
In \(\triangle ABC\), \(AB=AC\). Points \(D\) and \(E\) lie on \(AB\) and \(AC\), respectively, and \(AD=AE\). If \(BE=6\), find the length of \(CD\).
In \(\triangle ABC\) and \(\triangle DEF\), \(\angle A=\angle D\), \(\angle B=\angle E\), and \(BC=EF\). Which congruence criterion can be used?
In \(\triangle ABC\) and \(\triangle DEF\), \(\angle A=\angle D\), \(AB=DE\), and \(\angle B=\angle E\). Which criterion establishes congruence?
In \(\triangle ABC\) and \(\triangle DEF\), \(\angle A=\angle D\) and \(AB=DE\). Which additional condition allows the two triangles to be proved congruent by ASA?
In \(\triangle ABC\) and \(\triangle DEF\), \(\angle A=\angle D=50^\circ\) and \(\angle B=\angle E=60^\circ\). What is the measure of \(\angle F\) in degrees?
In \(\triangle ABC\) and \(\triangle DEF\), \(\angle A=\angle D\), \(\angle B=\angle E\), \(AC=DF=5\), and \(BC=4\). Find the length of \(EF\).
Why can SSA be used here for right triangles? (This refers to the fact that two right triangles are congruent if their hypotenuses and one pair of legs are respectively equal.)

choices.A: Because a pair of corresponding right angles is already equal, equal corresponding hypotenuses and legs form a special case of SSA, namely HL
choices.B: Because any two triangles are congruent if two sides and the angle opposite one of those sides are respectively equal
choices.C: Because the two acute angles of a right triangle are complementary, all three pairs of corresponding angles are equal
choices.D: Because the hypotenuse of a right triangle is always the shortest side

displayedInputs.question: Two right triangles have equal corresponding hypotenuses and one pair of equal corresponding legs. Which criterion establishes that they are congruent?
For two right triangles, which of the following conditions requires using HL to establish their congruence?

choices.A: Both pairs of corresponding legs are equal
choices.B: One acute angle and the hypotenuse are respectively equal
choices.C: The hypotenuse and one leg are respectively equal
choices.D: One acute angle and one leg are respectively equal

displayedInputs.question: In right triangles \(ABC\) and \(DEF\), \(\angle C=\angle F=90^\circ\), \(AB=DE\), \(AC=DF\), and \(\angle A=35^\circ\). Find the measure of \(\angle E\) in degrees.
In quadrilateral \(ABCD\), \(\angle C=\angle D=90^\circ\), \(AC=BD=8\), and \(BC=6\). Find the length of \(AD\).
Given \(AB=AC\) and \(AD\) is a median, which criterion is used to prove \(\triangle ABD\cong\triangle ACD\)?
In \(\triangle ABC\) and \(\triangle DBC\), \(BC=BC\) (common side), \(\angle ABC=\angle DBC\), and \(\angle ACB=\angle DCB\). Which criterion is used to prove that the two triangles are congruent?
In \(\triangle ABC\), \(AB=AC\), and \(AD\) bisects \(\angle BAC\), meeting \(BC\) at \(D\). The criterion for proving \(\triangle ABD\cong\triangle ACD\) is:
In \(\triangle ABC\), \(AB=AC\), and \(D\) is the midpoint of \(BC\). Find the measure of \(\angle ADB\) in degrees.
In right triangles \(ABC\) and \(DEF\), \(\angle C=\angle F=90^\circ\), \(AB=DE\), and \(BC=EF\). Which criterion should be used to prove congruence?
Which congruence criterion underlies the construction of an angle bisector?

Construct an angle equal to a given angle using a straightedge and compass: mark off \(OC=OD=4\text{ cm}\) on the two sides of the given angle, and measure \(CD=3\text{ cm}\). On one side of the new angle, mark \(O'C'=4\text{ cm}\), then construct \(O'D'=4\text{ cm}\) and \(C'D'=CD\). What is the length of \(C'D'\) (in cm)?

To construct the bisector of \(\angle AOB\) using a straightedge and compass, first draw an arc centered at \(O\) that meets \(OA\) and \(OB\) at \(C\) and \(D\). Then draw arcs with the same radius centered at \(C\) and \(D\), meeting at \(P\) inside the angle. To ensure that the two arcs intersect, this radius must be:

Use a straightedge and compass to construct the bisector \(OP\) of \(\angle AOB\) (\(OC=OD\), \(CP=DP\), and \(P\) lies inside the angle). If \(\angle AOB=70^\circ\), find the measure of \(\angle AOP\) in degrees.
Point \(P\) lies on the bisector of \(\angle AOB\). Its distance to \(OA\) is \(3\). What is its distance to \(OB\)?
In the angle bisector property, “the distances from a point to the two sides of the angle” refers to:

choices.A: The distances from the point to the endpoints of the two sides
choices.B: The lengths of the perpendicular segments from the point to the two sides
choices.C: The distance from the point to the vertex
choices.D: The distances from the point to any points on the two sides

displayedInputs.question: \(OP\) bisects \(\angle AOB\), \(PD\perp OA\) at \(D\), \(PE\perp OB\) at \(E\), \(PD=3x-2\), and \(PE=x+6\). Find the value of \(x\).
In right triangle \(ABC\), \(\angle C=90^\circ\), \(AD\) bisects \(\angle BAC\) and meets \(BC\) at \(D\), \(DE\perp AB\) at \(E\), \(BC=12\), and \(BD=7\). Find the length of \(DE\).

In \(\triangle ABC\), the bisectors of \(\angle ABC\) and \(\angle ACB\) intersect at \(P\). The distance from \(P\) to \(BC\) is \(3\), and the perimeter of \(\triangle ABC\) is \(18\). Find the area of \(\triangle ABC\).
If point \(P\) is equidistant from the two sides of \(\angle AOB\), must \(P\) lie on the angle bisector (\(P\) lies inside the angle)?

choices.A: Yes, it must lie on the angle bisector
choices.B: Not necessarily; it also depends on the distance from \(P\) to the vertex \(O\)
choices.C: Not necessarily; it lies on the angle bisector only when \(\angle AOB\) is a right angle
choices.D: No, it definitely does not lie on the angle bisector

displayedInputs.question: Point \(P\) lies inside \(\angle AOB\), and its distances to \(OA\) and \(OB\) are both \(5\). If \(\angle AOB=60^\circ\), find the measure of \(\angle AOP\) in degrees.
“A point inside an angle that is equidistant from its two sides lies on the angle bisector” is an angle bisector:
Point \(P\) lies inside \(\angle AOB\), \(PD\perp OA\) at \(D\), \(PE\perp OB\) at \(E\), \(PD=PE\), and \(\angle DOP=25^\circ\). Find the measure of \(\angle AOB\) in degrees.

When proving the angle bisector criterion theorem, given \(PD\perp OA\) at \(D\), \(PE\perp OB\) at \(E\), and \(PD=PE\), which criterion is used to prove that right triangles \(POD\) and \(POE\) are congruent?
Given that \(AD\) is a median of \(\triangle ABC\), how can extending the median to twice its length be used to prove \(AB+AC>2AD\)?

choices.A: Draw a line perpendicular to \(AD\) and prove that two right triangles are congruent
choices.B: Draw a line through \(D\) parallel to \(AB\) and use the equality of corresponding angles
choices.C: Take the midpoint \(E\) of \(AB\), join \(DE\), and use the triangle inequality
choices.D: Extend \(AD\) to \(E\) so that \(DE=AD\), prove \(\triangle ABD\cong\triangle ECD\), and then use the triangle inequality

displayedInputs.question: Extend median $AD$ of $\triangle ABC$ to point $E$ so that $DE=AD$. If $AD=4$, find the length of $AE$.

$AD$ is a median of $\triangle ABC$, with $AB=9$ and $AC=5$. Extend $AD$ to $E$ so that $DE=AD$, and draw $CE$. This gives $CE=AB$. After using the triangle inequality in $\triangle ACE$ to find the range of $AE$, how many values can $AD$ take if $AD$ is an integer?
When proving a sum or difference relationship between segment lengths, such as $a=b+c$, which auxiliary construction method is commonly used?

choices.A: Extend a median to twice its length
choices.C: Cut the longer segment or extend the shorter segment

displayedInputs.question: $AD$ is a median of $\triangle ABC$. Extend $AD$ to $E$ so that $DE=AD$, and draw $CE$. If $AB=7$, find the length of $CE$.
